title: How to conquer Kuttenberg
summary: Bypassing Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2's main quest by taking Kuttenberg myself.
body: Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is about a lad named Henry and his small role in kicking Sigismund of Luxembourg out of Bohemia in the name of the imprisoned King Wenceslas I. Henry and his newfound pals conspire, heist, assassinate, and sabotage to loosen the usurper's grip on the economic stronghold of Kuttenberg, but what they never try is barging straight in the front door. Just take the damn city! It can't be that hard. I say around 20, 40 men tops could do the job. In fact, if the story quests won't do it, I will. Step 1: Raise an army (Image credit: Warhorse) Surprisingly, this is the easy part. KCD2, for all its freedoms, does not natively allow Henry to roam Bohemia with a warband, so the mod " Companion Squad " from Steam user Triget will be the engine powering this righteous campaign. With just two keystrokes, my army began to take shape in front of me: 10, 20, 30 mercenaries with unique names and faces stood at attention, ready to attack at my command. The gates of Kuttenberg stood before us—doors wide open—its treasonous protectors oblivious to our plans. title: At last: I can build a home out of raw Windows Vista-era nostalgia
summary: Frutiger Home is a house builder for those who yearn for the glossiest time in tech.
body: Imagine for a moment: It's the year 2007. All software looks like glossy, rounded plastic, dewy glass, and photographs of verdant fields. Every electronic device makes ethereal chimes when it starts up. You've never heard the phrases 'live-service,' 'large language model,' or 'prediction market.' It's safer here, amidst the dreamy lime greens and ocean blues. It's better. And now, thanks to a new house-builder that launched on Steam this week, we can live the definitely-healthy fantasy of retreating into the security of yesterday's software aesthetics. Frutiger Home is a home decorating sim where you can build an impregnable psychic cocoon out of the finest design elements of an era where technology could still feel optimistic, and not like perpetual cognitive radiation poisoning. Hooray! All its architectural themes, available color swatches, and interior accent pieces are inspired by the Frutiger Aero aesthetic—a term retroactively coined by Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute co-founder Sofi Xian to describe the glossy, glassy, gleaming visual language that dominated tech and UI design from the mid-2000s to the early 2010s. title: Resident Evil's executive producer explains the deeper meaning behind Requiem, and I just can't get on board
summary: I'm gnawing at the bars of my enclosure.
body: I was brought up with the mindset that when you start something you should see it through to the end, even if it gets a bit tricky. So perhaps that's why Resident Evil dropping its in-built Roman numerals irks me so. It all started with Resident Evil: 7 Biohazard where the Roman numerals for seven were shoved into the 'E vil ' and then continued with Resident Evil: Vill age . So, in the lead up to Resident Evil 9 I was on tenterhooks, eager to find out how Capcom was going to incorporate IX into its title. I had my own theories , settling on Helix or Appendix as my favourite options. It made sense in my head, what with their respective links to DNA as well as the T-virus, and an icky body part that simultaneously means something that comes at the end of a story—I really liked appendix. Alas, we didn't get either or those—we didn't get an IX at all—we got Resident Evil Requiem . (Image credit: K.C. Green) I made my peace with Requiem, it has cool connotations for the game, referring to a prayer for the soul of the deceased or a general act of remembering someone who has died. I also saw one promotional image that turned the 'q' in Requiem into the number nine, so that's something, …

title: Arc Raiders' is taking no prisoners when it comes to cheaters with permanent bans becoming the new normal: 'No warnings. No second chances'
summary: Embark is really pulling out all the stops for Frozen Trail.
body: Embark is bringing forth a monumental effort ahead of Arc Raiders' anticipated major Frozen Trail update scheduled for next week . The devs have teased a bunch of new features like a temporary PvE mode , loot hotspots that change places, and a chance to build a base Topside , among a huge bevy of new items and arcs . And while I've been suitably hyped for all of this the issue of rampant cheating has still been in the forefront of my mind, Embark has now addressed this too . "Cheating undermines what makes Arc Raiders challenging and fun, and disrupts the experience for everyone playing fairly," executive producer, Aleksander Grøndal says in a blog post . "At Embark, we take it incredibly seriously, and spend a lot of time and money in the ongoing fight against unfair play. (Image credit: Embark) "The market for cheats is constantly evolving. Cheat makers profit from selling to players, often bundling malware with their software, and every time we improve our defenses, they adapt and find new ways around them. We adapt too. Our growing anti-cheat team is continually working to detect and block new cheats, close the pathways they exploit, and add obstacles that make cheating harder…

title: I want to punt Meta's Muse AI mascot back into the cursed void from whence it came
summary: Laser-targeted cuteness for everyone and no one.
body: I hate the new mascot for Meta's Muse AI assistant. The company unveiled the fluffy creature, as well as the Tamagotchi-esque Muse Charm device it will call home, (plus a VR headset that isn't really a VR headset ) during its yearly Meta Connect conference last week. The goal with Muse is to offer an AI assistant that "you can talk to in real time and reach in more places throughout your day," according to Meta . User's own Muse avatars can look wildly different , but the furry fiend default avatar that has so offended me is the company face of the entire Muse operation. The mascot's name is 'Jolly' on account of its "jolly and completely customizable character and personality," according to company CEO Mark Zuckerberg (via NBC News ). I hate that this little freak has inspired such a depth of feeling in me. I mean, just look at it. It also doesn't help that it looks a bit like a Doctor Who creature, the Adipose . Whenever I see this thing, I just think about that one scene where a character screams as she explodes into a puddle of sentient fat. title: Have you heard of the critically acclaimed MMORPG… oh, Final Fantasy 11, that's new
summary: The FF11 trial follows in the FF14 trial's footsteps.
body: Final Fantasy 14's free trial is massive—so massive, in fact, that it's become a bit of a copy/pasted meme over the years. The sentence "have you heard of the critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy 14" is burned into our brains. And, to be fair, it's a bloody huge one, currently letting you play for free for as long as you want right until the end of Shadowbringers (with some big limitations, mind). Still, it's a few hundred hours without a single monthly sub payment. Well, Final Fantasy 11's gonna be following in those footsteps, per the FF11 site: The site also mentions that previously-created trial characters will also be able to once again play the game, so if you started a free trial and ran out of game time, you can hop back in. That's a pretty huge bump—especially since it also lets players do some of the "Limit Break" quests. For context, while FF11 technically caps out at level 50, players can up that to a maximum of 99 by doing a certain questline every few levels. And they'll have all the time in the world to do it in, hooray! Honestly, this now makes two of Square's premier MMOs very generous—and as a fan of the genre writ large, I'm happy to see genuine efforts mad…

title: AMD's new 'Gainsborough' APU rumoured to be the chip that powers the long-awaited Steam Deck 2
summary: As Final Fantasy 7 fans will know, it's 'Gainsborough' because 'Aerith Gainsborough'.
body: The original Steam Deck went on sale about four and a half years ago. And there hasn't been any clear indication that a true second-gen handheld from Valve is imminent. Until now, that is. YouTube channel Moore's Law is Dead has a new video explaining how a rumoured AMD APU known as Gainsborough is likely to be the chip that powers the next-gen Steam Deck 2 handheld. The MLID channel is admittedly not everyone's cup of tea, but has had some notable hits over the years when it comes to leaks and rumours. With that caveat covered off, what do we know about Gainsborough? First, the codename does actually make sense. The OG Deck's APU was known as Aerith, as in the character from Final Fantasy 7. And Aerith's second same is, of course, Gainsborough. In terms of the technicalities, there isn't a huge amount of information. However, one critical tidbit is that it will be built on TSMC's N3P node. That's TSMC's fanciest, most advanced and most efficient version of its N3 family of chip production nodes. That matters because it should make for a more efficient chip for a handheld where battery life is critical. The immediate question is whether this makes sense given what Valve has said a…

title: Micron CEO says it'll be tougher to get memory in the next couple of years than it is today, and keeps saying it over and over again
summary: Alright, I get it already.
body: The head honcho of Micron, Sanjay Mehrotra, says that memory may be even harder to come by in the next two years than it is today. Now, a memory company's CEO is gonna say stuff like that during a historically momentous upturn in its business— anything to the contrary would be bad news for its share price—but it is a stark warning for all of us regular consumers still feeling the burn of the memory crisis. "Industry demand has strengthened since our last earnings call," says Mehrotra during the company's Q4 earnings call (transcript from Investing.com ), "and we expect memory and storage supply demand conditions to be much tighter in fiscal 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026." Here's Mehrotra again later in the call: "We expect memory and storage supply-demand conditions to be much tighter in calendar 2027 and 2028 than they were in 2026." And again… "As we noted, in calendar 2027 as well as 2028, we see demand exceeding supply." Alright, thanks, Mehrotra. "We have shared with you that we do not see line of sight when supply catches up with demand." Enough! title: Agony! Two life sims I really want to play launched back to back
summary: How do you choose to spend your time when two games you've been waiting for show up at once?
body: Nivalis Nights Everyone's been waiting years for this cyberpunk "slice of life" and shop sim and I'm logging my nightly progress as my noodle bar empire begins. I enjoy a good shop sim, especially when there's decorating to do too. Nivalis Nights is moody and neon-drenched and has a deeper shop finances simulation than I was expecting. I may be sinking a lot of hours into this! Songs of Glimmerwick This is the wizard school game made specifically for me. It's sort of in the Stardew vein of life sim with gardening and a seasonal schedule. I liked the Songs of Glimmerwick demo I played this year quite a lot . I really enjoy all the voice acting and its musical take on magic but I especially like its hopeful message about a world emerging from a generation of regressive politics.

title: The Americans have officially renamed artificial intelligence to 'Super Intelligence,' which should fix everything
summary: We're one step closer to "Super Earth" becoming a real thing.
body: Yup, it's real. They did it. Here's the full executive order , if you want to take it all in. Pity poor Sports Illustrated. It's laughable, up there with similarly demented efforts to rename the Gulf of Mexico , Lake Ontario , and maybe New Mexico —I guess we'll see how that one ultimately shakes out. It's also pretty funny how "super intelligence" jibes with "Super Earth," the fascist homeworld of humanity in Helldivers 2 . Probably just a coincidence, though. Yet somehow, I'm not inclined to laugh. That the leader—ruler, really, at this point—of the most powerful nation on the planet can just whip out bizarre ideas like this and have them treated seriously is kind of frightening, isn't it? And it is being taken seriously, at least insofar as we can describe billionaire tech oligarchs lining up to say and do pretty much whatever it takes to keep juicing the share price as seriousness: A subsequent White House Accord on Super Intelligence was signed by a who's-who of people who have made PC gaming almost impossibly expensive: Sundar Pichai (Google) Dario Amodei (Anthropic) Mark Zuckerberg (Meta) Greg Brockman (OpenAI) Elon Musk (XAI) Jensen Huang (Nvidia) (Image credit: Getty Imag…

title: Thanks Logitech, your new AI-fueled game clipping software makes me look trash at Counter-Strike, but I'mma keep it installed
summary: It works pretty well as a little manual recorder and editor.
body: Last week in Warsaw I got to see a first glimpse of Logitech's new Replay software , which is currently in beta. It records your game, and then lets you use its deep learning (technically not AI, I know) to figure out the best clips and splice them together for you. It looked pretty neat, from what they showed me, but I've just tried it in Counter-Strike and hoo boy does it have a way to go. If you watch the above vid, you'll notice a distinct lack of anything impressive. I jumped into a CS2 deathmatch, then played half of a casual game. From those two games, the software: Kicks off with me being spawnkilled Includes a random, unimpressive awp kill in the casual game's warmup round Shows a clip of me looking at the ground in spectator mode, already dead Includes plenty of missed shots Now okay, that's a little unfair. It does include some kills in there, but they're not great ones. In the deathmatch in particular—which the software only included a couple of clips from—I got some pretty dope kills later in the game, if I do say so myself. Including Deagle kills, Scout quickscopes, and even a flick noscope. Don't believe me? I thought that might be the case. So I went back into CS2 …
